paquet:commissariats:P1.summary:
P1 is finished. Six of the seven stations hold fixed vehicle bays checked against the real Paris map; the 3rd, 9th and 8th needed their door moved or a pedestrian-street exception (see deviations). The new data and validation tests pass and the type check is clean.

What exists now:
- **src/world/commissariats/data.ts** (pure data, no three.js):
  - The 7 sites (Préfecture/caserne de la Cité, Célestins, 1er, 3e, 7e, 8e, 9e) with the decision D4 stock: 32 vehicles. The car_crs and the vl_commandement at the Cité are non-engageable. Labels and call signs are in French.
  - The fixed bay layouts (FROZEN_LAYOUTS) were generated by layoutYard and pasted in, rounded to 0.1 m and 0.001 rad. Running the generator again gives exactly the same text.
  - Exports: COMMISSARIATS, commissariatById, nearestCommissariat, reservedBays, fileCentre, BAC_COLOR, VEHICLE_LEN, VEHICLE_WIDTH, STOCK_CALLSIGN_PATTERN.
- **src/world/commissariats/layout.ts** (used by tests only, never by the game):
  - SLOT_RULES, using the traffic module's own parking constants.
  - layoutYard: finds the door from the real façade by raycast and slides it along the same street if needed; reuses the station's street if parking is allowed there, otherwise the nearest eligible street within 150 m on foot; one file per unit, nose to the exit, at least 30 % spare bays; exit point 25 m downstream.
  - validateSite: checks door, façade, opening in front of the door, curb bays, clearance from junctions and crossings, parking rule, overlaps, the walk from the door to every bay, and the exit routes to Concorde and République with the road width sampled along them.
  - Also slotRing, slotsOverlap, pathWidthOk, exitWidthRules, printFrozen.
- **src/world/commissariats/held.ts**: isHeldVehicle(ctx, id). It returns false when the 'police.commissariats' service is absent or has no holds().
- **src/world/commissariats/index.ts**: re-exports the pure data and the helper.
- **src/gameplay/commissariats/api.ts**: types and constants only (service and system ids, the three events, EntryState, StockEntryView, CommissariatView, EngageResult, RecallTarget, CommissariatsApi, documentation of extra.commissariats and extra.renforts).

Where the bays ended up:

| Site | Bays on | Door to bays |
|---|---|---|
| Cité | boulevard du Palais | 9–48 m |
| Célestins | boulevard Henri-IV | 11–23 m |
| 1er | rue des Petits-Champs and avenue de l'Opéra | 151–167 m |
| 3e | boulevard de Sébastopol | 123–148 m |
| 7e | rond-point du Bleuet-de-France | 128–146 m |
| 8e | Champs-Élysées | 169–191 m |
| 9e | boulevard Haussmann | 114–127 m |

contracts.ts and extensions.ts are untouched. The interrupted previous agent had left only exploration scripts (tests/unit/zz-explore-comm*.test.ts); I used them and then deleted them.
paquet:commissariats:P1.testsRun:
- `npx vitest run tests/unit/commissariats.data.test.ts tests/unit/commissariats.sites.paris.test.ts` → 2 files passed, 16 tests passed, 1 skipped (the skipped one is the generator, which only runs with CRS_COMMISSARIATS_PRINT=1).
- `CRS_COMMISSARIATS_PRINT=1 npx vitest run tests/unit/commissariats.sites.paris.test.ts --silent=false` → 5/5 passed; all 7 sites reported "valide"; the printed layouts are byte-identical to FROZEN_LAYOUTS (diff).
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` → exit 0, no errors.
- No existing test file covers these new files, so no other suite was run.
deviations: The plan asked for an open arc of 90° or more with 25 m rays in front of the door. That is impossible on narrow real streets: rue Chauchat measured 55°, rue aux Ours 70°, the place du Marché-Saint-Honoré 55°. The rays now reach 25 m, or only to the far sidewalk when the street is narrower (2 × the door's distance to the street axis + 2 m, at least 8 m; doorRayLen). The 90° threshold is unchanged, so a courtyard or a recess still fails. Plan rule (b) is also applied literally: when the address façade fails, the door slides along the same street (±60 m). This moved the 3e door 17 m and the 9e door 16 m.

The plan asked for a road width of 6 m or more on the whole route for engines (water cannon, Centaure, coach). The real map data makes that impossible: the one-way pont au Change is 5 m (every route north from the Cité) and the two-way boulevard du Temple near République is 5.2 m. The rule is now: 5 m or more everywhere for every vehicle. Engines also need 6 m (two-way) or 5 m (one-way) on the first 400 m of their exit (SLOT_RULES.engineExit, exitWidthRules).

pathWidthOk takes two optional extra arguments (minimum for one-way roads, distance limit). It samples segment midpoints and ignores points more than 1.5 m off a road axis, so a narrow side street touching a junction is not misread as the route.
YardSlot gained a `width` field (vehicle width), used for the overlap test and later for the painted bays.
VEHICLE_LEN for vl_commandement is 6.6 m, not the plan's 5.0, because the real definition is 6.5 m long. VEHICLE_WIDTH and SPARE_LEN/SPARE_WIDTH (6.0 × 2.1 m bays) were added.

8e: the real door is on the pedestrian avenue du Général-Eisenhower. The 8e base (-535,-130) is more than 120 m from both the Eisenhower door and the Grand Palais's Winston-Churchill façade, so the seed has `pedestrianStreet: true`. The door is on the Grand Palais north façade (104 m from the base), the bays are on the Champs-Élysées, and "door within 18 m of a road" accepts named pedestrian streets (not footways). The address reads « 1, avenue du Général-Eisenhower (Grand Palais) ».

1er and 9e: the whole row of bays did not fit on any one stretch of curb between junctions. The generator therefore places unit by unit (each unit's file stays in one piece, spare bays two by two) on the nearest valid curbs. The 1er bays use two streets, so bayStreet reads « Rue des Petits Champs et Avenue de l'Opéra ».

Added a guard: no bay more than 200 m from the door (slotMaxFromDoor). The plan's 150 m limit applies to the distance from the door to the street, not to each bay. The 8e bays end up 169–191 m from the door, the 1er bays 151–167 m.

Call signs of the two non-engageable vehicles: « CAR CRS 1 » and « PC MOBILE 1 » instead of « PC MOBILE DOPC », so that every call sign matches one pattern (STOCK_CALLSIGN_PATTERN). Their labels keep the explanation (« PC mobile de la DOPC · hors dispositif »).

Kinds: the five arrondissement sites are 'commissariat_central' with sign 'commissariat', the Préfecture is 'prefecture' with sign 'none', the Célestins 'caserne_gendarmerie' with sign 'gendarmerie'. The union members 'commissariat' and 'hotel_police' are kept as in the plan but no site uses them (« hôtel de police » is not the Paris term).

The 6 journée bases were already moved by another team (for example the 1er is at 781,-211 and the 8e at -535,-130). The doors follow those bases (within 120 m, checked by the data test); the bases themselves were not touched.

data.ts also exports COMMISSARIAT_SEEDS, FrozenLayout and assembleCommissariat (seed plus frozen layout), so the generator and the frozen data share one source. layout.ts is not re-exported from index.ts, so the game never bundles the generator; the tests import '@/world/commissariats/layout' directly.
openIssues: P2: StockSeed.crew is a display count (section 18, peloton 18, BRAV-M 12, patrol car 3, Centaure and water cannon 3, prisoner van 2). P2 should check it against the units actually built.

P2/P5: at the 1er the units' bays are on two curbs (rue des Petits-Champs, then avenue de l'Opéra on both sides). fileCentre stays correct per unit because each unit's file is in one piece. The station-wide `exit` is computed from the first unit's curb.

P2: the Cité bays run from z 1171 to 1243 on boulevard du Palais, so they include the journée base point (1760,1225) where the company's vehicles park. This is expected: the plan says P2 skips occupied bays and falls back to spare bays.
P6 can use YardSlot.width for the painted bays.

To regenerate the layouts after a map change: `CRS_COMMISSARIATS_PRINT=1 npx vitest run tests/unit/commissariats.sites.paris.test.ts --silent=false`, then paste the printed FROZEN_LAYOUTS object into src/world/commissariats/data.ts.

paquet:commissariats:P3.summary:
P3 is finished. All its parts are in place, and the 3 new test files plus 8 existing related test files pass. `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` runs clean.

This step was about the commissariat feature's simulation side, not the command-map redesign you asked for. The plan says another team is doing that redesign. Nothing here adds buttons or changes the command map.

What exists now:
- **Reserved parking spots for police units** (src/sim/police/api.ts, units.ts):
  - Units can now be given a list of parking spots. Sections, pelotons and BRAV-M are placed exactly on them, at ground height, with crews aboard. Single vehicles with their crew (createEquipage) are placed on the first spot.
  - If there are more vehicles than spots, the extra ones go through the usual search, which checks every nearby vehicle, so nothing overlaps.
  - The prisoner van is not moved to the back of the group when spots were given.
  - Without spots, placement is unchanged.
- **BAC car crew:** an equipage of type 'voiture_bac' gets call sign « BAC n » and three plain-clothes officers: a brigadier-chef who leads and makes arrests, a driver, and a second arrest officer. It uses the unmarked BAC car when that vehicle type exists, otherwise a marked police car.
- **Rest:** a new `rest(squadId)` on the police units service sets fatigue to zero for the unit and all its sub-units. It also clears pressure, disorder and the relief request, and raises morale to at least 0.8.
- **Columns without sirens** (command/api.ts, convoy.ts):
  - A column destination can now say `urgence: false`. Every outbound drive then runs without siren or lights, at traffic speed, and any siren or lights left on are switched off when the order is given. The radio says « sans urgence » instead of « deux tons ».
  - Civilian cars blocking the column are not removed from the road.
  - The default is unchanged: sirens on. The leaving-the-site step (`depart()`) is untouched.
- **Patrol cars sent out from a station or sent home** (src/gameplay/patrols):
  - New state 'au_poste' (« Au poste »): the car stays parked in its spot and makes no radio reports until it gets an order. Orders then work as they do for a normal patrol.
  - `deploy(kind, callsign, home, at, homeAt?)` places the car exactly on its spot with three crew aboard and the brake on, in state 'au_poste'. It works in missions too, where no patrols are created automatically, and uses the session's seeded random generator.
  - `sendHome(squadId, at, by?)` cancels the current order, switches lights off and drives back without sirens. The map label reads « Retour au poste » and the car reports on the radio. Within 15 m of its spot, or when the autopilot reports arrival, it manoeuvres into the spot, switches to 'au_poste' and reports « Au poste, … équipage disponible ».
  - The car-creation code was moved into a shared function used by both normal patrols and `deploy`. A BAC patrol gets the unmarked car when it exists. With the same seed, the normal patrol setup gives exactly the same result as before (checked against the HEAD version, below).
paquet:commissariats:P3.testsRun:
- `npx vitest run tests/unit/police.parking-slots.test.ts`: 5/5 pass.
  - Section (AQUILON 1, Cité), peloton (ÉPERVIER 9, Célestins), mounted BRAV-M (FAUCON 9, 9e) and the Cité prisoner van end up within 0.05 m and 0.01 rad of their spots, everyone aboard, no overlaps.
  - With fewer spots than vehicles, the extra vehicles do not overlap anything.
  - Without spots, positions follow the unchanged placement rule and are identical between two runs.
  - `rest()` works.
  - The 'voiture_bac' crew is 3 plain-clothes officers aboard.
- `npx vitest run tests/unit/police-command.convoi-sans-urgence.test.ts`: 2/2 pass.
  - With `urgence: false`: siren 0/265 samples and lights 0/265 while moving; the civilian car is still there; the column reaches 'en_place'.
  - Default: siren on in 244/244 samples.
- `npx vitest run tests/unit/patrols.deploy.test.ts`: 3/3 pass.
  - Mission session (count() = 0): `deploy` gives 'au_poste', 3 aboard, `voiture_police`.
  - The car moves less than 0.5 m and says nothing on the radio for 900 s.
  - `send()` to République: siren 81/81, 'sur_place'.
  - `sendHome()`: lights 0, back to 'au_poste' in 262 s, 0.2 m from its spot, heading off by 1°.
  - BAC: 3 plain-clothes officers. With the same seed, 5 normal patrols come out identical.
- One-off regression check (temporary files, deleted afterwards): a copy of the HEAD patrols system and the new one ran 120 s on the same seed and gave identical patrol positions, states and targets (1/1 pass).
- Existing tests, all pass:
  - integration.patrouilles, police.unites, police-command.convoi, police.fourgons-places: 4 files, 9 tests pass.
  - ui-command.after-convoy, integration.colonnes-bravm, police-command.unites-speciales, police-command.commandement: 3 files pass and 1 is skipped as usual; 19 tests pass, 5 skipped.
  - patrouilles.equipage-hors-combat: 1/1 pass.
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p .`: exit 0, no errors.
deviations: The route-start call inside `arrive()` when `boardFirst` is false (convoy.ts, about line 299) was already non-urgent and is left unchanged. Making every outbound call follow `urgence` (default true) would have switched sirens on for an existing caller. All other outbound calls in `arrive` follow `dest.urgence`; `depart()` is unchanged.

Non-urgent columns drive each vehicle as a one-vehicle column instead of a plain drive. Measured: the autopilot only passes a stopped or parked vehicle when it is urgent or in a column, so a non-urgent stagger column stayed behind a parked van for the whole 420 s test. As a one-vehicle column it goes round, still without siren. Urgent columns are unchanged.
While a patrol is driving home, its state is 'en_route' with the label « Retour au poste », not a new state. The plan's data model only adds 'au_poste'.
On arrival, `sendHome` asks the autopilot to park the car (`park()`) in its exact spot and heading, so it does not stay in the traffic lane. The plan only said to switch to 'au_poste'.

`sendHome` first issues a 'libre' order that the patrol system itself ignores, so the map stops showing the old target. The police module then acknowledges it on the radio (« REÇU, je reprends ma mission »), as the existing patrol timeout already does. My own message is « Retour <home>, sans urgence », without a second « Reçu ».
When a patrol is 'au_poste' it also makes no radio reports. The plan only said its think step does nothing.
A patrol that goes out of action while 'au_poste' returns to 'au_poste' when its crew is fit again, not to normal patrolling.
`rest()` also clears the unit's pressure and disorder and marks its published status as stale, so the next read shows the reset values.
Tiny edit outside my file list: src/gameplay/patrols/index.ts now also exports the new type `PatrolPose`.

Tests on the real Paris map use mode 'libre': in headless runs, mode 'test' loads a small test district. The mission case uses mode 'carriere' with missionId 'crs-01-premier-samedi', because GameMode has no 'mission' value.
openIssues: P2: placing vehicles exactly on given spots does not depend on loaded map tiles. The fallback search for vehicles beyond the given spots does: it found nothing near the Cité until the tiles there were loaded. P2 should give at least as many spots as vehicles, as the plan intends, or accept fewer vehicles back from the handle.

P2/P5: call `deploy(kind, callsign, home, at, homeAt)` with `home` written the way the radio should say it (« commissariat du 9e »). The radio texts are « Retour <home>, sans urgence » and « Au poste, <home>, équipage disponible ».
P2: a patrol counts as arrived home when `statusOf(id).state === 'au_poste'`. After `sendHome` the car finishes parking within a few seconds of that switch.
P7: when the « modes » team adds the `voiture_bac` definition, BAC patrols, `deploy('bac')` and `createEquipage('voiture_bac')` will use it with no other change. The tests accept both vehicle types.

paquet:commissariats:P4.summary:
P4 is finished. Police roles now see the seven stations on every map: each station's door has a blue symbol showing how many units are available, and its name appears when you zoom in. Vehicles parked in a station's reserve no longer show up as loose vehicles in the unit list. The new test passes and the type check is clean.

**What the player sees** (map files in /tmp/claude-0/hunt/commissariats/crs-simulation/src/ui/maps/):
- **Symbol:** a navy rounded square at the door with « P » (police station), « PP » (Préfecture) or « G » (gendarmerie), a tricolour bar, and a green badge with the number of units available (grey at 0, « 9+ » above 9). It is drawn after the metro layer and before the GPS, orders, units and incidents (symbols.ts, overlay.ts).
- **Name:** shown under the symbol when zoomed in (below 2.5 m per pixel) or when the station is focused, without the address: « Commissariat du 9e », « Préfecture de police ».
- **Bays on another street:** when a station's parking bays are on a different street, a second line says so, for example « véhicules : Boulevard Haussmann ». It appears only when the station is focused or very zoomed in (below 1.2 m per pixel), to keep the map uncluttered, as the player asked.
- **Mini-map:** a smaller symbol (radius 5.5 px) with no text and no number in the badge.
- **Who sees it:** police roles only. Nothing is drawn without the stations service, when the module is inactive, or when the « Commissariats » layer is switched off.

**Data behind it:**
- **scene.ts:** the map scene keeps a list of stations, re-read at most twice per second from the stations service (type-only import). It records the door, available, engaged and resting units, the number of engageable units (the coach and mobile command post are not counted) and the bay street.
- **units.ts:** the list of service vehicles not attached to a unit skips vehicles parked in a station's reserve. The unmarked BAC car gets the same patrol-car symbol as the marked police car.
- **icons.ts:** a new « building » icon for P5's tab.

**Extras for P5 (overlay.ts):** a helper that finds the station under a click, tap or keyboard cursor within a pixel tolerance (14 px, or 22 px on touch, are P5's values). P5 also gets the station's display name and the size constants. symbols.ts adds a cached icon image of the symbol for the station list (empty outside a browser).
deviations: `commissariats` is a required field of the map layer mask, set to true in the all-layers default, not optional as the plan wrote. If it were optional, the existing layer toggle in tacticalScreen.ts would stop compiling as soon as P5 adds the layer, because the value would no longer be a plain true/false. Every layer mask in the code is built from the all-layers default, so nothing else changes.

The plan asked for an 11 px radius in compact mode. In the code, compact means the mini-map, so I used a smaller 5.5 px symbol with no text there, and 9 px on the tactical map and city map. The bigger touch target on phones belongs to P5's pick tolerance (22 px on touch) and can use the station-finder helper I added.

The scene record has one extra field, the bay street ('' when the bays are on the station's own street), so the map can show « véhicules : <rue> » as the plan's player experience (3.1) describes. It is read from the frozen data in '@/world/commissariats'. Its `total` counts only engageable units, so the coach and mobile command post at the Cité are left out.

Additions beyond the plan, for P5: the station-finder helper, the station display name, the size constants, the letters helper, the symbol colours, and exporting the vehicle-symbol function (the test needs it).
The scene reads the service by its string key 'police.commissariats' with a type-only import of the API, the same pattern as held.ts. This avoids loading the game module from the UI.
openIssues: integration.convergence-nasse.test.ts fails at line 151 (too few people leave through the filtered exit). I could not compare with the code before my changes because git stash is forbidden. Likely causes are the crowd simulation or the police/patrol files currently modified in this worktree. The map scene there is only read, and my additions do nothing without the stations service.

P5: the tactical screen's « Couches » list does not yet have the « Commissariats » toggle (the layer is on by default). P5 should also set the focused station on the map options and use the station-finder helper for picking.

paquet:commissariats:P6.summary:
P6 is finished. All seven police sites are now dressed in 3D on the real buildings, and the module is ready for P8 to plug in. It is not yet listed in src/main.ts (that is P8's job), so the player won't see any of it until then.

What exists now (src/render/commissariats/):
- **api.ts**: the service key 'render.commissariats', the stats (sites, built, visible, farVisible, drawCalls, triangles) and a nightOverride used by the test bench.
- **atlas.ts**: one shared 1024×512 painted texture. It holds a sign plate per site (« COMMISSARIAT DE POLICE » with « 9ᵉ ARRONDISSEMENT », the ordinal as a real superscript; « GENDARMERIE NATIONALE / CASERNE DES CÉLESTINS »), lantern faces « POLICE » and « GENDARMERIE », the lettered door glass for each, the « RÉPUBLIQUE FRANÇAISE / Liberté Égalité Fraternité » plaque, the yellow bay marking with « POLICE » (car size and motorbike size) and a white square for plain parts. The layout is plain data, so the UVs are also known under Node; under Node no texture is painted and vertex colours are used.
- **build.ts**:
  - buildSite() makes 2 merged meshes per site:
    - the façade: door frame 2.6 × 3.0 m with lettered glass, stone step, 2 bollards with white bands, sign 4.2 × 0.7 m, plaque, blue lantern on an iron bracket with 4 glass faces that light up, flag pole at 45° with a gold tip and the tricolour hanging from it (blue along the pole, red at the bottom, both faces). The Préfecture gets only the lantern and the flag, as decided.
    - the ground: one quad per bay, 2.5 cm above the drawn ground, with polygon offset.
  - buildFar(): one mesh for all 7 sites (lantern as 2 crossed squares plus the flag), 70 triangles in total. A per-vertex attribute hides a single site while keeping 1 draw call.
  - createMaterials(): 2 shared near materials (façade and ground; Lambert on quality 'bas') and 1 far material, all fed by one night uniform that is set once per frame.
- **system.ts**:
  - CommissariatsRenderer:
    - builds a site lazily within 450 m, at most one per frame;
    - shows the façade within 260 m of the door and the bays within 260 m of the bays (160 m on 'bas'). The two distances are separate because the bays are often 110–190 m away on another street;
    - shows the far mesh from 260 to 900 m (600 m on 'bas'), never beyond the draw distance, only while a site's façade is hidden;
    - rebuilds a façade when the drawn ground under the door changes (a city tile built later);
    - switches materials when the quality changes, and hides everything when inactive.
  - CommissariatsRenderSystem:
    - runs at order SystemOrder.VIEW and does nothing without ctx.view;
    - is active only when the loaded map is real Paris with every door inside it, the mode is not 'test', and extra.commissariats is not false;
    - reads the ground as world.heightAt + 'world.view'.liftAt, and the night from 'render.uniforms' (or env daylight as fallback);
    - frees the near dressing on 'session:ended' and in reset().
- **index.ts**: createSystems.

Test bench (harness/commissariats.html + .ts):
- the standalone view shows one site of each sign kind (9e, Célestins, Préfecture), with cameras porte / places / loin, day or night (keys 1–3, P, B, L, N, A, plus touch links) and the atlas;
- a « jeu » view runs the module on the REAL Paris map, with the real renderer, city and monuments.

All 9 real-map captures (all 7 sites, 9e at night and its bays) show the dressing correctly placed on the real façades and curbs.
deviations: Budget test, « every vertex within 30 m of the door »: this cannot hold for the ground mesh, because P1 put the bays 9–191 m from the door. The test checks it for the façade mesh, and checks that every bay vertex lies on its own slot. For the same reason, the system judges the bays' visibility by their own distance rather than the door's.

Flag: drawn with vertex-coloured stripes instead of a flag region in the atlas, so it looks the same with or without the texture. It hangs by its hoist along the 45° pole (blue along the pole, red at the bottom), as real façade flags do.

Célestins: the lantern and the door glass read « GENDARMERIE » instead of « POLICE », and the sign's second line is « CASERNE DES CÉLESTINS ». A blue POLICE lantern on a gendarmerie barracks would be a realism error.
The near/far switch is driven by the façade alone: a site appears in the far mesh while its façade is hidden, and stays there while the façade is not built yet (no blank zone).
The far lantern is a 2 m crossed square, bigger than the real 0.5 m lantern; it stands in for a glow so the light reads from 500 m.

Night emission comes from a shader patch (onBeforeCompile with an aGlow attribute) on the shared materials, not from a separate emissive material, so the near meshes keep 2 materials. Intensity is 1.6 at full night, weighted by aGlow: lantern 0.75, sign 0.45, door glass 0.35.
Not in the plan: the module is also hidden when the loaded map is not real Paris (synthetic test district) and in mode 'test', so the dressing never floats over the wrong map.
The plan's e2e asked for 390×844; that is what I ran, with quality 'bas' and touch emulation.
openIssues: P8 must register the module in src/main.ts after renderProps: `import { createSystems as renderCommissariats } from '@/render/commissariats';`. Without that the dressing never shows in the game. Only the harness runs it today.

P8 can add tests/e2e/commissariats.mjs to run-all.mjs. The default run uses the harness and takes about 1–2 minutes. `node tests/e2e/commissariats.mjs jeu` is the real-map check and takes about 10 minutes with software WebGL.
The relayed user request (too many buttons on the command map, needs to be clearer) is not touched by this package. Per the plan's addendum it belongs to the command-map redesign (PX/P5).

On the real map the door frame sometimes overlaps a ground-floor window of the real building (seen at the 9e and the 3e): the frozen door points from P1 are not aligned to the building's openings. It looks acceptable in the screenshots. Moving a door would be a P1 data change.

paquet:commissariats:P2.summary:
P2 is finished. It is not the command-map redesign you asked about in this request: P2 is the simulation behind the commissariats feature, and the plan gives that redesign to another team (package PX, then P5). Nothing here adds buttons or changes the command map.

The service 'police.commissariats' now works. It is not yet registered in src/main.ts; that is P8's job.

**Parked stock**
- When a session is set up, the 32 stock vehicles are parked on their fixed bays at the 7 sites. Each one is police, locked, empty, engine off, with the brake and handbrake on.
- Before parking, the service checks each bay for any vehicle or fixed obstacle within 0.4 m. If the bay is taken, it uses a spare bay. If none is free, the vehicle is "virtual" and is created when its unit is engaged.
- `holds()` is true for these parked vehicles. A parked vehicle leaves the stock when someone gets in, when it is wrecked or burnt, or when it is removed. A one-vehicle unit that loses its vehicle becomes « Indisponible ».
- The module is off in 'editeur' and 'test' modes, and when extra.commissariats is false. With extra.renforts false the stock is visible but nobody can engage.
- Only a commandant, a commissaire or a player of rank commandant or above can engage. Refusals come with a French reason (« Seul le commandant engage les moyens des commissariats », « Moyens fixés par l'ordre d'opération », …).

**Engage**
- `engage()` removes the parked vehicles and builds the real unit on exactly the same bays, crew aboard:
  - Police secours and BAC cars go through `patrols.deploy()`;
  - AQUILON 1 through `createSection`, ÉPERVIER 9 through `createPeloton`;
  - FAUCON 9 through `createBravm`, mounted, renamed « FAUCON 9 » with pairs « FAUCON 9-1 »…;
  - water cannons, Centaures and prisoner vans through `createEquipage`.
- If a van was taken from a section or peloton, the extra van is removed and its occupants board the others.
- Engaging twice returns the same unit. The unit goes « En alerte », and the radio says « … ICI TV 75-19. Équipage prêt au commissariat du 9e, en attente de destination. PARLEZ. ». The 'commissariat:engaged' and 'commissariat:stock' events fire.
- The default order is 'avancer' for a patrol car, 'colonne' for the BRAV-M and 'faire_mouvement' for the rest.

**States, checked every 0.5 s**
- « En alerte » becomes « Engagé » once the unit is more than 60 m from its bays; `where` then gives the sector name.
- A unit is « Indisponible » when all its vehicles are destroyed and fewer than half its crew can still act.
- « Au repos » becomes « Au poste » when the rest time is over, with a radio message.
- `atPost()` is true while the unit is au poste, en alerte or au repos. `entryOf()` and `isStationUnit()` also work for sub-units such as a single BRAV-M pair.

**Recall**
- `recall()` returns where the unit goes back:
  - the centre of its own row of bays;
  - for a patrol car, its first bay;
  - for any other unit: a patrol car goes to its own station; the journée company to its base station; anything else to the nearest station, using the spare bays.
- A recall given during a trip in progress is cancelled when the player gives a new order or starts a new column.

**Arrival**
- Arrival is detected from the column reaching 'en_place', a patrol car reaching 'au_poste', vehicles stopped near their bays, or the leader on foot within 40 m of the door.
- On arrival:
  - detainees still on board with custody 'in_vehicle' (never the player) get out and are removed;
  - the reserves of every vehicle are refilled and `units.rest()` runs;
  - the unit rests 120 s, or 300 s if morale is below 0.5;
  - the radio says « Arrivés à la préfecture de police, un interpellé remis à l'officier de police judiciaire, réserves complétées, équipage au repos 2 minutes »;
  - the 'commissariat:returned' event fires.
- When the autopilot can do it on the spot, a vehicle left a few metres off then manoeuvres into its exact bay.
- No 'law.handover' points are registered. Nothing uses random draws.
